text: The corridor ahead is watched. Twenty metres of it. I counted, and so will the sentry at the far end.
There is a second sentry in a cell over there, facing the wall. It is in disgrace. You may borrow it.
You keep walking down that corridor as if the sentry might change its mind. It will not. It has no mind. It has a colleague, though, and you know where that one is.
It never saw you. It will file a report saying a colleague walked up to it and sat down on the button. Nobody will read it. Nobody reads any of them.
They are bolted to the floor, so do not get ideas. The button is up on the ledge with the door. It wants something heavy. I am sure something heavy will turn up.
Those two have stared at those pillars every day for years. They have never once wondered what is on the other side. Neither, it seems, have you.
They shot each other, and you used one of them as a doorstop. I would report it, but that department was closed. Most of them were.
The receiver is in the roof of that tunnel. The laser is over there. They have never met. You are going to introduce them.
The door also wants the crate on its plate. The plate is through the tunnel. I am sure that will not matter at all.
Most people do this room twice. The first time, they light the receiver and then remember the crate. You are welcome to join them.
You sent light up through the floor, and you thought of the crate first. I had a speech prepared about doing things in order. I will save it.
The field runs wall to wall. You can walk through it. The crate cannot. Your portals will not survive it either.
The crate is on the far side. The plate is on this side. The door is on a ledge. You see the difficulty. You see most of it.
You have been staring at this side of the room for some time. The other side has walls too. Some of them face the other way.
The crate went through a wall without touching the field. That is called thinking with doors. I did not invent the phrase. I would have done better.
Two plates. Two crates. One sentry, in a booth, with a very good view of the lane. I paid extra for the view.
The door will open only when both plates are pressed. I did not invent this rule. I merely enforce it.
That sentry sees the whole lane through one small window. It cannot see through crates. I mention these two facts for no reason at all.
You blindfolded it with a crate. It is still watching, in its way. I find that I respect it.
It has spent its whole life looking at everything except itself. Some of my best people were like that. Show it the view.
The plate is past the field. The crate is not. The crate cannot go through the field. I have explained this to the crate.
The purple panel works for the whole room this time. I am feeling generous. It will not last.
Anything loose that falls up will go on falling up until something stops it. You know what that something is. You are holding the tool.
The crate fell up, came down somewhere else, and you caught it at the right moment. That is called timing. It is rarer than you would think.
You have done this before. I have since added a welcoming committee of one.
The crate is coming with you. How it travels is up to you. I know which way I would send it.
You keep arriving in front of that sentry and leaving in a hurry. Something should arrive before you do. Something heavy, and in a hurry.
You threw a crate at a colleague and walked in after it. That is the exam. You passed. I will not be telling you by how much.
